summary: Significance and venue-fit verdict, answering the three mandated questions explicitly. (1) Interesting enough for MNRAS: conditionally yes. The surviving contribution core -- the Eddington-in-z sigma_z^2 H0-bias law with its known-truth coverage-collapse demonstration, the prior-consistency invariant, the three discriminating observables separating information starvation from normalization bias, the pinned-version audit of four published pipelines, and a released deterministic calibration harness -- is a genuine, timely methods advance for galaxy-catalogue dark-siren cosmology, verified by Stage 2 as having no published counterpart and independently corroborated (not preempted) by the nearest prior work; MNRAS has direct topical precedent (Turski et al. 2023, the closest published study, is an MNRAS paper) and the subject sits squarely in its methods-for-astronomical-measurement scope. (2) Merely technically competent: no, but with a load-bearing split the current framing obscures. The paper's most dramatic empirical arc (rail at 0.86, flip to 0.60, de-rail to 0.73) diagnoses two defects that the paper's own audit shows are structurally excluded from every published pipeline -- self-inflicted implementation errors whose field value is prophylactic; that arc alone would be a competent code anecdote below the venue bar. What lifts the paper above it is the transferable half: the bare-Gaussian kernel bias that IS live in the flagship pipeline by an unenforced declaration, the coverage methodology, and the validation-gap map. (3) Overclaimed relative to the actual contribution: yes, in three specific and repairable dimensions. First, the significance backbone designates sigma_z/z ~ 0.7 as 'the regime probed here', but no evidence bundle in the paper occupies it: the coverage calibration lives at sigma_z/z ~ 0.1-0.2, the real-data sample is mostly near-spectroscopic, and its catalogue-dominated character is an artifact of the pre-dt2 shallow depth -- the gap the paper names remains open, including by this paper. Second, the novelty narrative predates Cross-Parkin et al. 2025 (uncited, known-truth, photometric, Gray-family, volume-prior, unbiased), which falsifies the introduction's implicit universal and forces the gap statement down to its narrower three-part conjunction. Third, the abstract's 'calibrated close to nominal' is scoped only to the clean single-host limit while the full-completion-machinery coverage is 0.40/0.54/0.82 -- in tension with the paper's own prescriptive conclusion that coverage tests are field prerequisites. Additionally the headline demonstration is literally incomplete ([RESULT PENDING] full-grid confirmation). Recommendation ceiling: major_revision -- not reject, because the required repairs narrow the claims without changing the central result (the rail is a curable prior-consistency artifact, not information starvation; the bare kernel collapses coverage; the volume kernel repairs it), and the narrowed paper still clears the MNRAS significance bar; not minor, because the overclaims sit in the abstract, introduction, and conclusions -- the significance backbone -- and one central result slot is unfilled.
strengths: Genuine, corroborated novelty core: the Eddington-in-z sigma_z^2 bias law for dark-siren H0 and the known-truth coverage-collapse demonstration have no published counterpart (Stage 2 adversarial search through 2026), and the nearest adjacent study (Cross-Parkin et al. 2025) independently finds the volume prior unbiased -- corroborating rather than preempting the contribution.

Venue fit in kind is strong: MNRAS publishes exactly this class of catalogue-method calibration work (Turski et al. 2023 on GLADE+ photometric-redshift modelling in gwcosmo dark sirens is MNRAS), the technical depth and 21-page length are appropriate, and the GW-cosmology readership is native to the journal.

Transferable value beyond the anecdote: the prior-consistency invariant ('every population measure counted exactly once, identically in numerator and selection normalization') is cheap for any implementer to check; the three discriminating observables (railing vs broadening, sigma_z^2 bias vs width growth, invariance under estimator repair) make the misdiagnosis analysis reusable; and the released deterministic P-P harness is a community tool, not just supporting evidence.

The pinned-version code-and-paper audit of four pipelines is a real service contribution that converts a private failure into field-level information, and it is honest in both directions (gwcosmo structurally excludes the rail; the bare kernel is nonetheless live there by declaration).

Unusual claim hygiene at the mechanics level -- per-number artifact sourcing, disclosed unfavourable items (dt2 scale defect, timeout selection, Omega_m fiducial), and explicit simulated-events scope statements -- which makes the surviving significance trustworthy once the framing is narrowed.

The prescriptive closing recommendation (known-truth coverage tests at photometric width deserve the standing of the spectroscopic mock data challenges) is actionable, defensible, and likely to be cited as a standard to meet, independent of the specific pipeline story.

findings.summary: The significance backbone rests on a regime designation the paper never occupies: the abstract sells 'sigma_z/z ~ 0.7 in the GLADE+ regime probed here' and 'the regime that LISA-era dark sirens ... will occupy', but the coverage evidence lives at sigma_z/z ~ 0.1-0.2, the real-data sample is mostly near-spectroscopic, and the sample's catalogue-dominated character is a by-product of the pre-dt2 shallow depth -- so the paper's central selling point (closing, or even probing, the order-unity-ratio validation gap) is not what the paper delivers.
findings.rationale: This is the significance-stage consequence of REF-R002/REF-P001/REF-P005, which I adopt as established: the known-truth calibration occupies the perturbative Eddington regime, the non-perturbative sigma_z/z ~ 0.7 regime is never coverage-tested by anyone including this paper, and per the paper's own budget a corrected-depth EMRI campaign on GLADE+ would be completion-dominated, so the 'catalogue-dominated' conjunct silently assumes future LSST/Euclid-depth catalogues. The honest, still-publishable contribution is 'we demonstrate the mechanism class, the repair, and the calibration methodology at photometric absolute width, and we map the untested regime'; the abstract currently invites the stronger reading 'we probed the regime the field will occupy'. For a paper whose venue case is its field-level warning, this gap between advertised and delivered regime is the difference between a significant methods paper and an oversold one, and an MNRAS referee reading abstract-first will find it.
findings.required_action: Rewrite the abstract, introduction, and conclusions so the regime bookkeeping is explicit: state which sigma_z/z each evidence bundle occupies, present the sigma_z/z ~ 0.7 regime as the mapped-but-still-open gap (open for this paper too, unless a non-perturbative coverage run is added per REF-P001), and recast the headline contribution as mechanism-plus-methodology at photometric absolute width rather than as probing the LISA-era regime.

findings.summary: Venue-readiness concurrence: the full-scale confirmation of the headline de-rail (all 3375 events, complete 38-value grid, volume-deconvolved default) is an explicit [RESULT PENDING] placeholder, so the significance of the paper's central real-data demonstration cannot be finally adjudicated -- no venue accepts a manuscript whose headline confirmation slot is unfilled.
findings.rationale: Concurs with REF-R001/REF-M002 and registers the significance-stage consequence: the de-rail evidence currently rests on a 494-event subsample and a seven-point grid whose injected truth coincides with the grid midpoint (REF-P002), so the pending full-grid run is not a formality but the demonstration's completion. If it lands as expected (interior peak near 0.73), the significance case stands as assessed here; if it does not, the de-rail narrative -- and with it the paper's venue case -- must be revised, not patched.
findings.required_action: Fill the placeholder with the actual full-grid combined-posterior result before any submission decision, and re-check the abstract's de-rail sentence against it.

findings.summary: The novelty-and-significance framing must be rebuilt around the uncited Cross-Parkin et al. 2025 and the 2025-2026 adjacent literature before the venue case can be evaluated as stated: the introduction's implicit universal (photometric-redshift studies exist only on real data where bias cannot be tested) is falsified, and the abstract's 'known-truth validations are almost entirely spectroscopic' is strained -- the gap statement survives only in its narrower three-part conjunction (known-truth AND catalogue-information-dominated AND order-unity sigma_z/z).
findings.rationale: Concurs with REF-L001/REF-L002 and adds the significance adjudication: the narrowed claim is still a real and interesting gap, and citing Cross-Parkin is strictly favourable to the paper (their volume-prior unbiasedness at sigma_z/z <~ 0.08 independently corroborates the repair; their spectroscopic-vs-photometric trade-off strengthens the motivation). But because the negative universal is the paper's significance backbone, restating it correctly is a substantial reframing of abstract, introduction, codes section, and conclusions -- not a citation insertion -- and until it is done the paper claims more novelty than it owns. A negative-existence claim at MNRAS also needs the explicit adjacent-work map (Blinded MDC I, Borghi et al. 2026, CHIMERA v2, Alfradique et al. 2025) that REF-L002 specifies, so the claim reads as 'here is the complete map and the cell is empty' rather than 'we found nothing'.
findings.required_action: Execute the REF-L001/REF-L002 repairs (three-way taxonomy of known-truth validations, adjacent-studies passage, full-conjunction gap statement everywhere it appears) and re-derive the abstract's significance sentences from the narrowed claim.

findings.summary: Two of the three diagnosed defects (peak-density sky factor, global-denominator tilt) are self-inflicted implementation errors that the paper's own audit shows are structurally excluded from all four published pipelines, so the manuscript's most dramatic empirical arc -- rail up, flip down, de-rail -- carries prophylactic rather than direct field-level significance; the paper's genuinely field-live result (the bare-kernel Eddington bias present in gwcosmo by an unenforced declaration, -3.3 per cent on H0 at sigma_z = 0.035 with coverage collapse) is quieter but is the actual venue case, and the current abstract/introduction weight the drama toward the rail.
findings.rationale: Anti-conflation check this stage exists for: the difficulty and drama of the internal failure-and-repair arc must not be mistaken for field significance. The paper itself states the correct split (codes.tex's 'two precise halves': the rail is a hazard of independent implementation; the bare-kernel bias is live in the flagship pipeline), and the prophylactic half has real value in an era of multiplying independent implementations -- but the abstract leads with the rail numbers and the introduction's 'field-level hazard for every independently implemented dark-siren pipeline' phrasing (already flagged by the proof red-team as a narrowed universal) inflates the anecdote's reach. If a revision foregrounds the transferable elements (invariant, bias law, coverage methodology, audit) and presents the rail as the case study that exposed them, the paper clears the MNRAS bar comfortably; if the rail remains the headline, a referee can fairly ask whether the core is a code post-mortem.
findings.required_action: Rebalance the abstract and introduction so the two halves of the field-level statement get proportional weight: lead the significance case with the bare-kernel bias law, coverage collapse, and validation gap (the live, general results), present the rail arc explicitly as the exposing case study, and scope the 'every independently implemented pipeline' hazard sentence to the ex-ante/future-implementations reading the conclusions already use; fold in the REF-P004 mechanism-attribution fix, since the misattributed sigma_z^2 invisibility currently props up the hazard claim's generality.

findings.summary: Venue-fit conditionality: MNRAS fit is good in kind (direct topical precedent, methods scope, appropriate depth), but the 'LISA-era' motivation is carried by a mock population that is not a LISA-era population -- a physical-SNR >= 200, z <~ 0.11 sample produced by the pre-dt2 scale defect -- so the astrophysical-realism expectations of an MNRAS referee are met only if the sample is consistently presented as a controlled estimator testbed rather than a representative EMRI campaign.
findings.rationale: The dt2 self-consistency argument is physically sound (REF-P005 adjudicated) and the estimator-comparison logic survives; the residual venue risk is presentational: 'LISA-era dark sirens will occupy this regime' motivates significance in the abstract and conclusions while the analysed configuration exists only because of the scale defect, and the corrected-depth campaign is deferred to Paper B. One or two sentences making the testbed status explicit wherever LISA-era framing appears (and noting the future-catalogue depth assumption per REF-P005) removes the exposure; without them, the significance framing borrows realism the sample does not have.
findings.required_action: Add the REF-P005 sentence connecting the dt2 caveat to the regime designation, and audit every 'LISA-era' occurrence to ensure it reads as motivation for the methodology rather than as a description of the analysed sample.

findings.summary: Proportionality tension between the paper's prescriptive significance claim and its own evidence: the conclusions elevate known-truth coverage tests at photometric width to a field prerequisite, yet the paper's own full-completion-machinery coverage test returns 0.40/0.54/0.82 with a compressed MAP-vs-truth slope -- i.e. the adopted estimator would not pass, at nominal, the very test the paper prescribes, and the residuals are attributed to the synthetic's modelling rather than demonstrated to be.
findings.rationale: Concurs with REF-R003/REF-P002 and registers the significance-layer consequence: the prescription itself is one of the paper's most valuable exports, so it must be stated in a form the paper itself satisfies -- calibration demonstrated in the clean single-host limit, full-machinery calibration an open task for every pipeline including this one. As written, a referee can turn the paper's own standard against it; scoped honestly, the same fact becomes evidence for how demanding (and needed) the standard is.
findings.required_action: Scope the calibration claim to the clean single-host limit wherever it appears at abstract/conclusion level, and phrase the coverage-test prescription so that full-machinery calibration is explicitly named as open for all pipelines including this one (or add the REF-P002 ablation/off-centre-truth experiment that would close it).
